passage: I'm Isha, and I was sitting two rows behind when a lab assistant told Manoj, in front of everyone, that people from his part of the country "never finish on time." Manoj went still. Dhruv shot to his feet. "I'm going straight to the head of department. Right now. I'll sort this out for you." I saw Manoj tug his sleeve, and I saw a flicker cross Manoj's face that I can't name. Dhruv stopped. He sat down, took a breath and asked, "What do you want here? Tell me and I'll back you." Manoj said quietly that he wanted to speak to the coordinator himself. On Friday they went together. Manoj talked and Dhruv stood a step behind him, saying nothing at all until Manoj looked over.

qa.q: What did the lab assistant say about people from Manoj's part of the country?
qa.a: The lab assistant said they "never finish on time."

qa.q: Why did Dhruv stop and sit down after Manoj tugged his sleeve?
qa.a: Dhruv seemed to realise he was speaking over Manoj and wanted to ask what Manoj wanted, though Isha says the reason cannot be known for sure.

qa.q: What did Dhruv do that supported Manoj's voice?
qa.a: He asked what Manoj wanted, then stood a step behind while Manoj spoke to the coordinator himself.

qa.q: How might Manoj have felt if Dhruv had gone straight to the head of department?
qa.a: Manoj might have felt helpless or sidelined, as though the situation had become Dhruv's story instead of his own.

grounding: A friend faces bias and the protagonist first wants to shield him, then asks what he wants and supports his own voice.
